title: Manipur’s Dr Thangjam Dhabali Singh Receives 17th O.N.E. India Award 2026
summary: Manipur's Dr Thangjam Dhabali Singh receives the 17th O.N.E. India Award 2026 in Mumbai for contributions to healthcare, tourism, employment generation and socio-economic development.
body:
MUMBAI: Manipur-based pathologist and entrepreneur Dr Thangjam Dhabali Singh has been conferred the 17th O.N.E. (Our North East) India Award 2026 in recognition of his contributions to healthcare, tourism, employment generation and socio-economic development in Manipur.

The award was presented by Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Arlekar at a ceremony organised by My Home India on November 17 at the Swatantryaveer Savarkar Rashtriya Smarak in Dadar, Mumbai.

The ceremony was presided over by Padma Shri awardee and renowned endocrinologist Dr Shashank Joshi. My Home India founder and former BJP national secretary Sunil Deodhar, who conceptualised the award, and the organisation's president, Dr Harish Shetty, were also present.

**From a Modest Beginning to the Babina Group**

Dr Singh began his entrepreneurial journey in 1983 with an initial investment of Rs 20,000. He subsequently established the Babina Group, which has expanded its activities across healthcare, hospitality and tourism.

Over the years, the group has contributed to the development of healthcare facilities and tourism-related infrastructure in Manipur, while creating employment opportunities for local people.

His work in healthcare has focused on strengthening medical services within the state and improving access to diagnostic and treatment facilities. His contributions have also been associated with efforts to reduce the need for patients to travel outside Manipur for specialised medical care.

**Contributions Beyond Healthcare**

Apart from his professional and business activities, Dr Singh has been involved in humanitarian initiatives, cancer screening programmes and social welfare activities.

He has also contributed to efforts to preserve historical heritage, including support for the development of the Imphal Peace Museum, which highlights the shared history of Manipur and Japan during the Second World War.

His work in promoting tourism and preserving historical connections has also contributed to strengthening cultural links between Manipur and Japan.

In recognition of his contribution to strengthening India-Japan relations, the Government of Japan conferred the prestigious Order of the Rising Sun, Gold and Silver Rays on him in 2020.

**O.N.E. India Award Recognises Contributions to Northeast**

Instituted by My Home India, the O.N.E. (Our North East) India Award recognises individuals whose work contributes to the development of the northeastern states and promotes national integration.

The 17th edition of the award brought together personalities from different fields to recognise their contributions to society and the region.

Dr Singh's recognition acknowledges his work across healthcare, entrepreneurship, tourism, employment generation and humanitarian initiatives. It also brings national attention to the role of Manipur-based institutions and entrepreneurs in contributing to the state's development.

The award marks another recognition of Dr Singh's professional and social contributions, particularly his efforts to expand healthcare and employment opportunities within Manipur.
author: Mirror Lilong Desk
